frequency_question: How often do riparian treaty renewals face structural impasses that prevent signing within the designated window?
membership_rule: Includes all bilateral river water allocation treaties involving sovereign states that required renewal or successor establishment due to fixed-term expiration clauses, excluding purely domestic water disputes.
window: Within the final 24 months preceding treaty expiration or immediately following lapse.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty (India-Pakistan permanent mechanism, continuous implementation)
Mahakali Treaty (India-Nepal successor to Tanakpur/Sharda arrangements)
Columbia River Treaty regime modifications and renegotiations (US-Canada)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase updates (Lesotho-South Africa)

coverage_note: 5 named major bilateral transboundary water treaty renewal processes; captures key South Asian and global comparable riparian negotiations.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller municipal-level basin agreements where stakes and structural frictions are vastly lower.
skeleton: Named historical riparian treaty renewal processes facing severe federal/sub-national friction.
validity_reason: Bilateral riparian negotiation norms and bureaucratic friction patterns evolve slowly over decades.
